messages:
Alex: Heads-up — noticed a p95 regression on canary + some NaN/Inf tokens coming out of the FP8 path after yesterday's kernel-selector change. Repro and logs below.
Maya: :eyes: saw spikes during the 10:30 canary push. p95 +30%, and ~0.08% responses had NaN tokens (literally 'nan' in model logits).
Jake: Can you paste the exact log snippet and the canary flags?
Alex: Sure. Canary flags: kernel_selector=v2, batcher_policy=aggressive, kv_prefetch=true. Log snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T10:31:12Z INFO request_id=abc123 model=rdx-7b-fp8 seq_len=2048 batch_id=1123 kernel=fp8_forward output_status=ok
2026-03-17T10:31:12Z WARN request_id=abc123 numeric=overflow scale=1.2e+38 token_idx=43
2026-03-17T10:31:12Z ERROR request_id=abc123 output=NaN token_idx=44
```
Priya: Repro steps that hit it reliably for me: run the local perf harness with `--model rdx-7b-fp8 --seq 2048 --batcher aggressive --kv-prefetch=true --seed 42` and 8 concurrent streams.
Tim: I ran pprof on the canary instance. High-level breakdown (median of samples): kernel_selector: 42ms, batcher_queue: 95ms, fp8_dequant+compute: 11ms, kv_merge: 18ms, memory_copy: 9ms. The spike correlates with batches that have a mix of cached KV + freshly computed blocks.
Zara: My hunch: when we merge KV cache (older prefix) with the new attention blocks we hit a numeric rescaling path that assumes similar scale distributions. FP8 has tiny headroom; a skew causes exponent overflow and then NaN.
Priya: Agreed. SmoothQuant helped on a different model earlier by stabilizing per-channel scales at dequant time. Two ideas: 1) clamp scales before dequant (min_scale=1e-6, max_scale=1e3) and 2) add a conservative fallback to INT8 when `kv_merge_flag` is true and seq_len>1024.
Maya: Short-term mitigation: disable FP8 kernel in kernel-selector for sequences >1024 in canary (fall back to int8/float16). Rolling that out now to stop customer impact. :thumbsup:
Alex: Proposed code change for kernel selector (sketch):
```
bool is_safe_for_fp8(int seq_len, float batch_scale_variance, bool kv_merge) {
  if (seq_len > 1024) return false; // conservative
  if (kv_merge && batch_scale_variance > 4.0f) return false;
  return true;
}
```
Plus emit telemetry event `numeric.issue.fp8.nan` with sample hashes.
Jake: Will attach a PR with gating logic + telemetry. Also add unit test that runs the merged-KV dequant path and asserts no NaN for a worst-case synthetic scale.
ci-bot: Build queued for alex/kernel-fp8-safety.
Priya: One more point — our online smoothquant calibration currently samples ~128 calibration batches, which isn't enough for rare long-prefix distributions. Suggest increasing to 1k samples and adding a periodic drift detector that triggers re-calibration when distribution KL>0.03 relative to baseline.
Tim: I'll run a calibration sweep across a few production traces overnight. If smoothquant with larger calibration fixes it, we can re-enable fp8 for canary with the new calibration. Timeline: patch + canary rollback within ~2 hours, full sweep results tomorrow morning.
Zara: Created incident INC-2026-0317 and added the thread to postmortems. Setting owner=Tim, sev=2 for now. :bug:
Alex: Thanks — keeping this thread as single source of truth. Follow-ups: Jake to open PR, Tim to post sweep results, Priya to draft calibration config, Maya to monitor canary rollback.
Maya: quick notes for postmortem: reproduce command, pprof flamegraph, offending batch ids, telemetry count for `numeric.issue.fp8.nan`.
Alex: Closing the loop — once rollback is stable we'll re-run the optimizer for kernel selection with the new safe-gating.
